Chapter 8: Healing in Fragments—Trauma, Memory, and the Long Road to Recovery.
Healing isn’t really a destination, is it? It’s more like a winding journey—filled with ups and downs, setbacks and small victories that aren’t always obvious to the people around us.
For Yazidi survivors, those old wounds are never really out of sight. They show up in nightmares, in sudden flashes of memory, and in those quiet times when the world just feels unbearably heavy.
Inside the camps, and in new places they now call home, healing can look different for everyone. Some folks find comfort in faith, turning back to rituals and prayers that once gave their lives structure. Others pour their pain into art, music, or writing—finding a kind of freedom through creativity.
And then there are those who reach out for therapy. They start learning to put words to their trauma, discovering new ways to cope.
Picture this—one evening, a young man sits across from a counselor, his hands shaking as he tries to talk about what he’s lived through. The words come slowly, but just saying them out loud brings a bit of relief. The counselor listens, no judgment, only understanding. For the first time, this young man feels truly seen. He realizes he’s not alone.
Healing almost never moves in a straight line. There are days when memories weigh too much, and the future feels out of reach. But then, there are moments of light—a child’s laughter, a meal shared with friends, a song sung in the old language. Those small joys? They become lifelines, little reminders that life can still be beautiful.
The community is everything. Survivors lean on each other, swapping stories and sharing ways to cope. Together, they create safe spaces to grieve, to remember, and to imagine new hope. It’s a slow process, and there aren’t any quick fixes. But just coming together, refusing to let trauma have the last word—that’s an act of resilience all its own.
Most people never see the invisible scars carried by survivors of violence. It’s easy to get caught up in headlines and forget about the daily struggle to heal. But for the Yazidis, healing is something they take on together—a way to honor what’s been lost and, at the same time, build something new.
The road is long. But every single step forward? That’s a victory.
